clue.text: Uncle's business is selling fizzy drinks

definitions.meaning: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, whose premises are slangily called this
a shop that sells pop, the fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker has branched out into soft drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so his business is a pawnshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang for a pawnbroker's premises, and literally a store trading in soda pop.

clue.text: Settled in advance for help with homework

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework
aid means help

explanation.surface: Paying ahead of time for someone to assist with schoolwork.
explanation.walkthrough: PREP is British school slang for homework (preparation).
explanation.definitionFit: Prepaid describes a bill paid before it falls due, settled ahead of time.

clue.text: Splitting up after splitting hairs

definitions.meaning: dividing the hair on the head along a line with a comb

explanation.surface: A couple separates after a petty argument over details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting hairs' wants to mean quibbling, but it is literal: the line combed through the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a separation, and the line where combed hair divides.

clue.text: Most memorable moments for mountaineers

parts.note: the best moments of anything, which for climbers would literally be the summits they reach

explanation.surface: Climbers recall their finest experiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The most enjoyable parts of an event are its highlights, and mountaineers literally seek elevated places.

clue.text: Innkeeper inclined to take advantage

indicators.note: the inclined word takes in the advantage word

parts.note: prone means inclined or liable
AD is tennis shorthand for advantage

explanation.surface: A landlord is likely to exploit his guests.
explanation.walkthrough: AD is the tennis score 'advantage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A padrone is an Italian landlord or proprietor of an inn.

clue.text: Daughter tucked into fruit taken from scarf

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside another, the daughter abbreviation going into the fruit

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: A daughter eats a piece of fruit she had wrapped in her scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large patterned kerchief worn round the head or neck, a kind of scarf.

clue.text: Major transaction doesn't impress me!

explanation.surface: An unimpressed reaction to news of a huge business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a large commercial arrangement, and a scornful retort meaning 'so what'.

clue.text: Assist an uppity woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, uppity means reading upwards, so both words are written backwards

parts.note: aid means assist

explanation.surface: Help a woman who is getting above herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppity' turns AID AN upwards, giving NA DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a female first name, so it fits a woman.

clue.text: Car rug obtained from slot machine

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A car rug was bought from a vending machine.
explanation.walkthrough: An automat is an American coin-operated cafeteria or vending machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An automat is a coin-operated vending machine dispensing food.

clue.text: She paid to annihilate such pests

indicators.note: annihilating something destroys its form, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener paid to have the pests wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphides is a plural of aphid, the greenfly and blackfly that plague gardens.

clue.text: Infuriated by voguish fashion in the end

indicators.note: the fashion word sits in the middle of the word for the end

parts.note: taken as the word end
a craze or the rage is the fashion of the moment

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at how a trendy fashion turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' reads as 'eventually', but 'in' is the container signal and 'the end' is the word taken literally; 'voguish fashion' is the current craze.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraged means being made extremely angry, which is to be infuriated.

clue.text: Leave one's wife to pay her share

parts.note: to go is to leave
'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: A man walks out on his wife, leaving her to pay her own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' as a wife comes from Cockney London slang, 'my old Dutch' (from duchess).
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is for each person on an outing to pay for themselves, so she pays her share.

clue.text: Farewell to Spain

parts.note: reads like bidding goodbye to the country, but means the goodbye spoken in Spain, literally 'to God'

explanation.surface: Someone bids a last goodbye to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Spanish word for goodbye, so it is the farewell used in Spain.

clue.text: Cordial Pam and doreen concocted

indicators.note: something concocted is made up from ingredients, so the letters of the two names are mixed

explanation.surface: Two women, Pam and Doreen, have mixed up a fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like a drink they concocted, but it is the adjective meaning warm and friendly; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial welcome is a warm, wholehearted one, just as a welcoming embrace is.

clue.text: It bloomed when Sirius was in the ascendant

parts.note: Sirius is the Dog Star
climbed into the sky, i.e. rose

explanation.surface: A flower blossomed when the brightest star in the sky was rising.
explanation.walkthrough: Sirius, the brightest star, is called the Dog Star; 'rose' doubles as the verb and the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing shrub whose pink flowers bloom in summer.

clue.text: Little one immersed in fairy tales? Understatement!

indicators.note: one piece is plunged inside the other, the small child going into the falsehoods

parts.note: fairy tales are lies, untrue stories
a tot is a little child

explanation.surface: Calling a small child's adventure merely a fairy tale is putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy tales' means fibs, LIES, not storybooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the rhetorical figure of understatement, such as saying 'not bad' to mean good.

clue.text: Basket of finest fare puts too much weight on decking

definitions.meaning: a luxury hamper of the best food
a nautical term for excess gear and rigging above deck

explanation.surface: A heavy luxury picnic basket overloads the patio.
explanation.walkthrough: In sailing, top-hamper is the masts and rigging that weigh a ship down above deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the best food basket, and the burdensome rigging weighing on a ship's upper deck.

clue.text: Mean as I may be, it made me forget

indicators.note: the words may be something else once their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their meanness by blaming a lapse of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the condition that makes a person forget.

clue.text: Object to item in the paper

definitions.meaning: a piece of writing in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a piece in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' looks like a verb of protest, but 'Object' is the noun thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a thing or item, and a written piece in a newspaper.

clue.text: Dashed back with speed to tell stories

indicators.note: back means the dashing word is read in reverse

parts.note: ran means dashed
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone hurried back quickly to tell tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount events or tell a story.

clue.text: Pole loved going round in decorative gear

indicators.note: the loved word goes round the pole letter

parts.note: adored means loved
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man in love is dressed up in finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorned is decorated, so a person adorned is dressed up in ornaments.

clue.text: I am to confront favourite American force

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to stand up to the American frontrunner.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving momentum or force behind something moving.

clue.text: Persuaded by Italian leader in India

indicators.note: the Italian leader is placed inside the India abbreviation

parts.note: Il Duce was the title of Mussolini

explanation.surface: Someone was talked round by an Italian leader in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Duce, 'leader', was Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade or prevail upon them.

clue.text: Her royal position proved a strain, sadly

definitions.text: Her royal position proved a strain, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters end up in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A queen finds her royal role a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges STRAIN to TSARIN, and the A stands beside it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was a Russian empress, whose regal role could well prove a burden.

clue.text: Feel inclined to doubt his innocence

definitions.meaning: to be inclined to think something true
to regard a person as possibly guilty

explanation.surface: Someone begins to question a man's innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to surmise or believe without proof, and to think a person possibly guilty.

clue.text: Produce grain by ancient doorway

parts.note: to thresh is to beat cereal to separate the grain
old means ancient

explanation.surface: A farmer threshes grain beside an old doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill at the foot of an entrance, so by extension the doorway itself.

clue.text: A shade sanctimonious in the main

indicators.note: the pious word goes inside the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Someone a little holier-than-thou is out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the high sea, and PI is short for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, a shade.

clue.text: Gather it's a minute pack-animal

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, used to carry packs

explanation.surface: A tiny donkey is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity.

clue.text: Swindle within swindle to get grappling-iron

indicators.note: the first swindle word goes inside the second

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket

explanation.surface: A fraudster pulls one scam inside another to obtain a climbing tool.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMP as a swindle is British slang for a racket or fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked iron plate fixed to a boot for gripping ice, a kind of grappling iron.

clue.text: Fancy putting charge on current account!

parts.note: C is the symbol for current in physics
A is the abbreviation for account
a price is a charge

explanation.surface: It is a whim to put a fee on someone's current bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting charge on' means PRICE goes after (on) C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim or fancy.

clue.text: Crooked dealer pockets many a jewel

indicators.note: one piece pockets another, holding it inside
a crooked arrangement is bent out of shape, so the letters of the dealer word are jumbled

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A dishonest trader slips many a gem into his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' scrambles DEALER to ERALDE, which 'pockets' M.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone, a gem.

clue.text: Don't besiege Sandhurst, even when inactive!

indicators.note: to besiege is to surround, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: Sandhurst is the Royal Military Academy, RMA

explanation.surface: A warning not to lay siege to the military college, even when it is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is Britain's army officer training college, the Royal Military Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means asleep or temporarily not active.
